title: The Wishing Well

subtitle.text: Moving is never easy.
Moving from a big city like Chicago to a small country village is even harder.
Just ask the Barth children.
"There's nothing to do here!" complained the oldest, named Cy.
"I don't see any shops," whined Anthea, the second eldest.
Among her siblings, her nickname was Panther.
When her younger brother, Bobby, was little, he couldn't say Anthea.
He called her Panther instead, and now the others did too.
[g@"What do you mean, we won't have Internet?"
cried Bobby, looking up at his father.@g]
"Eeek! What's that?" Jane screamed.
A little brown field mouse scurried from under the steps and into the grass.
No one in the family had wanted to move to Aunt Martha's house.
But Father had lost his job, and they had no choice.
[g@"It's only for a short while,"
Mother said, trying to comfort the children as they sat at the kitchen table.@g]
"And there're lots of things to do around here," said Aunt Martha.
[g@"Yeah, like catching grasshoppers?"
Cy said in a rather nasty way.@g]
"Grasshoppers? Where?" screamed Jane.
To make matters worse, Mother and Father left the next morning.
Father had some job interviews in Chicago.
The children stood alone on the steps as the car pulled away.
"Baa, baa," cried the baby happily.
"Oh, Lamb. Nothing makes you sad, does it?" Panther laughed.
Hilary, the baby, got his nickname because the first word he said was "baa," just like a little lamb.
The children didn't want to go back inside the house.
[g@There was nothing to do there.
Behind Aunt Martha's house was a thick forest.@g]
And since no one had a better idea, they set off to explore the woods.
"Look!" Bobby pointed excitedly at a family of raccoons.
"Smell these!" Panther said, as she bent over some colorful flowers.
All day, the children searched the forest for new discoveries.
After a while, they found themselves in a thicket of trees.
"It's awfully dark in here," Panther said in a worried voice.
"Maybe we should go back," Jane added.
"Hey! Look at this!" Cy called out excitedly.
Cy had found an old, dried-up well.
[g@"Can you see anything?"
asked Jane, as they all peered down the well.@g]
"Nope! But there's a funny smell," replied Cy.
"Is there any water?" Bobby asked.
The children stared deeper into the well, their eyes getting wider.
"I wonder if this is a wishing well," said Jane.
"Wait! Look here," said Panther.
Next to the well, Panther had found an old wooden bucket attached to some rope.
"Let's lower this bucket and see what's down there," she said.
"What's she doing?" Bobby said, pointing to Jane.
Jane's eyes were closed, and she was holding onto a coin.
"I'm making a wish," she replied.
She turned around and threw the coin over her shoulder and into the well.
[i@Clink, clink, clonk.@i]
"Ouch!" a voice cried from the well.
"Did you hear that?" whispered Bobby.
"Hello, down there!" Cy shouted.
[g@"Hello, down there!"
his voice echoed inside the well. Then silence.@g]
"I'm sure I heard something," said Bobby.
"Do you think it's an animal?" Jane asked worriedly.
"There's only one way to find out," Cy said excitedly.
He lowered the bucket down the well.
"Can you feel anything?" Panther asked.
"Hurry up, will you?" Bobby said impatiently.
Cy pulled the bucket back up.
It was full of mud, soda cans, an old shoe, and some rocks.
Cy lowered the bucket again several times.
If there was something in the well, he was determined to find it.
After a while, Cy got tired of lowering the bucket.
[g@The others wanted to give up, too.
Cy let out a deep breath.@g]
[g@"That's it. There's nothing else down there,"
he said, emptying a final bucket load.@g]
"Wait," cried Panther.
[g@"Look at this!"
She picked out an unusual shell covered in mud.@g]
"What is it?" Jane asked, looking closer.
[g@Panther wiped off some of the mud and held it up.
It was beautiful.@g]
"I think it's a seashell," she replied.
[g@She began wiping off the rest of the mud.
Suddenly the shell began to giggle.@g]
Panther was so shocked she almost dropped it.
"It laughed!" Bobby shouted loudly.
"Something's inside." He knocked on the shell.
"Ouch! Stop that!" the shell cried.
[g@The children all looked at each other.
Then the most amazing thing happened.@g]
[g@A creature poked its head out from the shell.
It had the face of a seahorse.@g]
On its neck and back were shimmery fins that opened and closed.
As its head circled left and right, the fins glowed and shone.
For the first time in their lives, the children were speechless.
"Well?" the creature asked in an irritated voice.
[g@Finally, Panther spoke up.
"What are you?"@g]
[g@The creature gazed at them.
"Let me get this straight," it began.@g]
[g@"You throw things on me and wake me up."
It glared at Jane.@g]
[g@"You start taking away my things."
It looked at Cy.@g]
[g@"You tickle me."
It stared at Panther.@g]
"Then you bang on my shell!"@g]
Bobby looked down at the ground.
"And now, you tell me that you don't even know what I am?"
The children stared at the ground in embarrassment.
[g@"We're sorry," apologized Jane.
"We didn't know you were in the well."@g]
[g@The creature didn't say anything.
After a while, its fins stopped glowing.@g]
"Apology accepted," it said finally.
"But we really don't know what you are," Cy added quickly.
[g@"I am Huit des Orlanes," it announced.
"The eighth of my kind of the sea."@g]
"Wow," the children said in unison.
"But you can call me Huey," the creature smiled.
It was clear from the children's blank faces that they still did not know what he was.
"Do you know what an Orlane is?" he asked.
"Not really," Jane admitted for them all.
[g@Huey closed his eyes dramatically.
His head turned quickly from side to side.@g]
"At one time," he said, "we Orlanes were the best-known mystic creatures of the sea."
"You mean, you're a fairy?" interrupted Bobby.
"A fairy? Oh, my, oh, my!"
Huey's fins started to glow again as they opened and closed quickly.
"Please don't be upset, Huey," said Jane.
"Bobby didn't mean to call you a fairy."
"All right then," Huey said calmly.
"Orlanes have the gift to grant others whatever they want," he continued.
"You mean you can make wishes come true?" Bobby asked.
Huey nodded, and the other children joined Bobby in shouts of delight.
[g@"However," Huey said in a loud voice.
"There are two things you must promise."@g]
"We'll do anything to get our wish!" Jane clapped her hands.
Huey continued. "First," he said, "you can only make one wish a day.
And second, after making your wish, you must return me to the well."
"That doesn't sound too hard." Cy laughed.
"By the way," Huey smiled, "at sunset, everything returns to the way it was."
"You mean, our wish is true only for one day?" asked Bobby in a disappointed voice.
"Yes," Huey replied, and with that he disappeared back into his shell.
The next morning, the children could hardly eat their breakfast fast enough.
They were excited about visiting Huey again.
"Where's the fire?" Aunt Martha asked.
Cy gave his siblings a warning look.
They had promised not to speak about Huey to anyone.
[g@"We're just going out to the woods today,"
Bobby said, his mouth full of pancake.@g]
The previous day, Cy had lowered Huey back down the well, just as Huey had asked.
And Bobby had cleverly marked the trail that led to the well.
But after searching for the trail for a while, they seemed to be going in circles.
"Are you sure it's this way, Bobby?" Jane whined.
"What did you use to mark the trail?" asked Panther.
"Peanuts," replied Bobby.
Unfortunately for the children, a family of raccoons had eaten Bobby's trail markers.
"Just great! We'll never find the trail!" cried Cy.
The children looked around in confusion.
"Let's try this path," Panther said.
They headed off in the direction she pointed.
Hours passed, but there was still no sign of the well.
"We're lost. We'll never find Huey now," complained Jane.
[g@"Wait! What's that over there?"
cried Cy, pointing and jumping up and down.@g]
"Look! We found the well!"
The children raced to the well.
Cy quickly lowered the bucket and pulled up the shell.
"Huey, Huey," they called together.
Huey's head slowly peeked out of his shell.
"Oh, it's you again," he said sleepily.
"I was hoping that meeting you had been just a bad dream."
[g@Panther decided to ask something friendly:
"Huey, how did you end up in this well?"@g]
"It may look like just an old well to you," Huey said.
"But this well is also a traveling station for sea creatures like me."
"Where are you going?" asked Jane.
"I am journeying to Marvesti to meet my brothers.
This well is only a temporary stop."
"You mean, you're going to leave?" Bobby wailed. "When?"
"When the time is right," Huey replied in a firm voice.
"Now, do you have a wish or not?"
In all their excitement, the children hadn't thought about what to wish for.
They looked at each other.
"I haven't got all day and neither do you," Huey pointed out.
"I think Cy should make the first wish," said Jane.
"Thank you, Jane," said Cy smugly.
"Why should Cy go first?" complained Bobby.
[g@While the three of them argued, Panther said softly to herself,
"I wish we were beautiful and handsome."@g]
Suddenly Huey's fins glowed pink and red.
They opened and closed gracefully three times.
The children stopped arguing and looked at Huey in amazement.
Then each of them felt a light, soft mist on his or her face.
"What's happening?" Bobby asked in a scared voice.
"Your wish is being granted," replied Huey.
"Our wish? What wish?" Cy asked, puzzled.
They felt the mist lift from their faces.
"Your wish to become beautiful and handsome," said Huey.
Cy, Bobby, and Jane looked at each other, and at Panther too, wondering what Huey meant.
But none of the children recognized the faces staring back.
Just as Panther had wished, each of them was as beautiful or handsome as a movie star.
The Barth children could not recognize each other.
"Cy?" Panther asked, reaching out to a young boy with dark, wavy hair and clear blue eyes.
[g@"Panther?" Cy said.
He touched a long wavy lock of her golden hair.@g]
Panther's hair was normally straight brown and quite plain.
"Does anyone have a mirror?" asked Jane.
[g@"What do I look like?"
Jane was absolutely beautiful.@g]
She had short red hair with little curls around her face.
Her skin was rosy, and she had bright, shining green eyes.
[g@"I don't know why anyone wants to be beautiful," complained Bobby,
"This was your idea, wasn't it, Panther?"@g]
[g@"Yes, I wished it," admitted Panther,
"but I'm glad to be beautiful for once."@g]
[g@"Good, lovely, and all that," Huey interrupted.
"Now, be off with you.@g]
[g@Remember that your wish ends at sunset."
Huey disappeared back into his shell.@g]
Cy carefully lowered him back down the well.
[g@The children walked into town.
Many people turned to stare at them.@g]
"I must be beautiful because everyone is looking at me," thought Panther.
Just then, she recognized Aunt Martha's neighbor.
"Look! There's Mr. Becker," she said.
Mr. Becker was walking his dog, Silver.
"Hello, Mr. Becker! Hello, Silver!" Panther called out cheerfully.
Panther, being an animal lover, had gotten to know Silver as soon as they had arrived at Aunt Martha's.
Now, however, neither Mr. Becker nor Silver seemed to recognize her.
"Woof! Woof!" Silver barked angrily.
"What's the matter, Silver? It's me, Panther!" she said.
Panther bent down to pet the dog's head.
"Be careful, young lady," Mr. Becker warned.
"Or else my dog might bite your hand."
Bobby faced his neighbor.
[g@"Mr. Becker, it's Bobby Barth!" he said.
"We live next door."@g]
Mr. Becker looked at each child suspiciously.
"I don't know who you children are," he said in a stern voice.
"But I've never seen you before in my life."
"But, but . . ." Panther stepped forward, attempting to explain.
Suddenly, Silver lunged.
Quickly Panther stepped back, but Silver had pulled the leash from Mr. Becker's hand.
Startled, the children all turned and fled.
Excitedly, the barking dog gave chase.
"Run!" yelled Cy.
The children ran toward their aunt's house.
"I hope Aunt Martha is home!" gasped Panther.
Luckily for the children, the front door was open.
"Hurry!" Cy shouted to his siblings.
He slammed the door behind them, just as Silver reached the steps.
The children collapsed onto the floor.
"That was a close call," Bobby sighed loudly.
[g@"Why did Silver chase me?
He loves me!"
wailed Panther, her beautiful eyes filling with tears.@g]
[g@"Because you look different,"
Cy pointed out, but it didn't help Panther feel much better.@g]
The children looked all over for Aunt Martha and Lamb.
[g@"She's not home,"
said Cy, as everyone followed him into the kitchen.@g]
"Maybe she went shopping?" said Jane.
"Well, I'm hungry," Bobby said.
[g@"I'm going to have a snack."
He opened the fridge.@g]
"I'm taking a shower," said Cy, heading for the stairs.
[g@"Come on, Panther." Jane held out her hand.
"Let's go get changed."@g]
Panther took a moment to study her brothers and sister.
Their voices sounded the same.
But when Panther looked at their faces, it felt as if she was in a house with strangers.
A little while later, Aunt Martha returned from shopping.
"That's strange," she said, noticing the dirty rug.
"Children? Are you home?" she called out.
"In here!" came a voice from the kitchen.
With a shopping bag in one arm and Lamb in the other, Aunt Martha walked toward the voice.
Bobby was eating his second peanut butter sandwich when Aunt Martha entered the kitchen.
"Oh, my!" she gasped, dropping the bag and almost dropping Lamb too.
"Who are you?" she shouted at Bobby.
[g@Bobby looked up from his sandwich.
"It's me, Aunt Martha," he said.@g]
But of course Aunt Martha did not recognize the boy sitting in her kitchen.
Aunt Martha hurried to put Lamb down, and Cy walked in, fresh from his shower.
"Hey, I'll have a sandwich now," he said to his brother.
[g@"What? Another one?" Aunt Martha exclaimed.
Alarmed, she grabbed a broom.@g]
"Aunt Martha," Cy tried to explain.
"I'm not your aunt!" she shouted.
[g@"And how do you know my name?"
She waved the broom in their faces.@g]
Upstairs, Panther was staring at the beautiful girl in the mirror.
"Panther, should I wear my pink blouse or my blue one?"
Jane called from the next room.
"I don't know. Pick your favorite," Panther replied carelessly.
Panther had grown up believing that she wasn't pretty.
"I would be so much happier if I was beautiful," she had always thought.
She turned her face to the side, still examining her reflection.
"Now I am beautiful," she said, as if to convince herself.
But who was the "self" looking back at her?
Jane walked in, interrupting Panther's thoughts.
[g@"Let's go down.
I hear Aunt Martha," she said.@g]
[g@Panther looked at her sister.
"Oh!" she said with a startled breath.@g]
"What is it?" asked Jane, looking around.
[g@Panther shook her head.
"Nothing, it's just . . ."@g]
"What?" asked Jane.
"I didn't recognize you," Panther replied, embarrassed.
Back in the kitchen, Cy and Bobby were in big trouble.
[g@"We're telling you the truth," Cy pleaded.
"I'm Cy and that's Bobby!"@g]
Aunt Martha was not going to let herself be fooled.
[g@"Do you think I'm stupid?" she said.
"You are not Cy, and you are not Bobby!"@g]
Just then, Panther and Jane stepped into the kitchen.
"Aunt Martha! What are you doing?" they cried.
For a second, Aunt Martha was stunned.
"How many more of you are there?" she shouted.
Aunt Martha's angry voice made Lamb cry.
Panther ran over to comfort her baby brother.
"It's okay, Lamb. Your sister is here," she said.
She tried to pick him up, but Lamb only screamed more loudly.
[g@"What's the matter? It's me!"
Panther said in a trembling voice.@g]
But Lamb's wide eyes said that he did not know her at all.
"You stay away from that baby!"
Aunt Martha said and swatted Panther with the broom.
[g@"Lamb?" Panther would not give up.
"It's your sister."@g]
Lamb howled again.
"I've had enough," Aunt Martha screamed.
[g@"Get out! All of you!
Get out of my house!"@g]
She lifted the broom and began swinging it around like a baseball bat.
The Barth children ran out, upset.
Not only Aunt Martha, but even baby Lamb did not recognize them anymore.
"I can't believe Lamb didn't know me," cried Panther.
[g@"Well, I hope you're happy," Cy said hotly.
"You wanted to be beautiful."@g]
"I don't blame Lamb," Bobby gasped.
[g@"Even I don't know you.
I don't know myself."@g]
The children sat huddled under a tree.
They were cold and hungry and had no place to go.
"I want to go home." Jane shivered.
"It's no fun being pretty if no one knows who you are."
"It's getting dark," Bobby said, pointing to the sky.
"What are we going to do?"
The children watched miserably as the sun began to go down.
[g@"Wait a minute," Cy blurted.
"Do you feel that?"@g]
They all felt a light mist on their faces, just as they had felt when they were with Huey that morning.
[g@They looked at each other cautiously.
"Panther! It's you!" Cy shouted joyfully.@g]
Exactly as Huey had said, the wish had ended as soon as the sun was set.
"Oh, I'm so happy to be me again!" Panther cried.
[g@Bobby added, "Me too.
Now let's go home and get something to eat!"@g]
Aunt Martha was waiting by the door when the children got home.
"Am I ever glad to see you," she said, giving them each a big hug and kiss.
She told them about the strange kids who had broken into the house.
"I nearly had a heart attack," she exclaimed.
"How they knew my name, I'll never know."
Dinner that evening was unusually quiet.
The children were careful not to say anything about Huey or their wish.
But once they were alone, they all spoke at once.
Cy held up his hand.
"Wait, wait," he said. "Panther, you go first."
"I want to say that I'm sorry about today," she said quietly.
"And I don't think we should go see Huey anymore."
[g@The others disagreed.
"That's not fair," complained Bobby.@g]
"I haven't had my wish yet."
"Yeah, I want a wish, too," whined Jane.
"I think it's only fair for each of us to have at least one wish," Cy agreed.
"So tomorrow, I'll go first─ "
"Hey, why do you get to go first?" interrupted Bobby.
[g@"Because I'm the oldest," said Cy.
"Next will be Bobby, and then Jane, okay?"@g]
The others nodded their heads.
Bright and early the next morning, the children set off to see Huey.
[g@"Well, well." Huey grinned.
"How did it feel to be handsome and beautiful?"@g]
"Fine, thank you," Panther answered quickly and untruthfully.
[g@"So what will you wish for today?"
he said, shaking out his fins and swiveling his head.@g]
"I wish," Cy said excitedly, "we were rich."
"How rich?" Huey asked.
Cy scratched his head. "Uh, well . . ."
[g@Huey pointed to the bucket.
"Enough money to fill this?" he asked.@g]
Cy rubbed his hands and said, "Twenty of those buckets, please."
"And would you like gold? Silver?" asked Huey.
[g@Cy scratched his head again.
"Gold," he answered.@g]
Huey spread his fins and they turned bright gold.
"Wow," Bobby whispered under his breath.
Like magic, twenty buckets appeared, and then gold coins showered down from the sky.
"It's raining gold!" squealed Jane.
[g@"How are we going to carry all this?"
Cy asked, pointing to the buckets now filled with shining coins.@g]
Closing his fins, Huey said, "That's your problem."
He ducked back into his shell.
"Don't forget—it'll all be gone by sunset," he added.
Cy lowered Huey down the well, and the children started to fill their pockets with the gold.
[g@"Take as much as you can," Cy urged.
"The more the better."@g]

episodes.title: All That Glitters Is Not Gold

subtitle.text: The children decided to go home and put their riches into bags.
Cy and Bobby put all their gold coins into a backpack.
"How will I know which ones are mine?" asked Bobby.
[g@"It doesn't matter," replied his brother.
"We can share."@g]
The girls decided to divide their money.
[g@"Panther, that's my gold coin,"
Jane said, grabbing a coin that fell to the floor.@g]
[g@"No, Jane. It's mine.
It fell out of my pocket," argued Panther.@g]
She snatched the coin from her little sister and put it into her bag.
In town, the children were excited by their new wealth.
"What are you going to buy first?" Bobby asked Cy.
"I'm going to get a hundred games so I won't ever be bored," he answered.
[g@"I'm going to buy a car,"
Bobby said with a sparkle in his eye.@g]
"You can't drive," Jane pointed out.
Bobby shrugged and said, "Doesn't matter.
I'll get a driver to drive me around."
[g@Cy stopped in front of a store.
"Here we are," he said.@g]
He lifted his hand toward the sign that read "Game World."
"I don't want to go in that store," said Bobby.
"Me neither," agreed Jane.
"I'm going to Dot's Dress Shop to look at skirts," said Panther.
The children began to argue about where to go first.
[g@Finally Cy raised both hands and said,
"We can all go wherever we want.@g]
We'll meet here after we've been shopping, okay?"
The others quickly agreed.
Cy walked into the game store alone.
His eyes fell on the rows and rows of games.
"Wow!" he said, sucking in his breath.
"Can I help you?" asked the store clerk.
[g@"Yes," Cy answered.
"I want one of every game in the store."@g]
Meanwhile, Bobby went to look at cars.
He fingered a two-door silver sports car.
"Are you looking for a birthday gift for your dad?" one car salesman teased.
"Maybe he's saving up to buy it in ten years," laughed another.
"More like twenty years," roared the other.
[g@Bobby held his head high and left the store.
"They'll see," he thought.@g]
Panther and Jane went to Dot's Dress Shop to buy some clothes.
The girls tried on many dresses and found one that they liked.
[g@"Jane, that's my dress,"
said Panther, pointing to the dress Jane was trying on.@g]
It was exactly the same one that Panther had on.
[g@"It's my dress.
I saw it first," Jane replied hotly.@g]
"Why don't you find another dress?" Panther said sweetly.
"Why don't you?" Jane replied nastily.
Back at the game store, Cy stood at the checkout.
He was counting all the new games that were soon to be his.
"Look, boy," said the clerk, "how are you going to pay for all this?"
"I happen to be a very rich man," Cy replied snobbishly.
[g@"Maybe you should show me the money first,"
the clerk said, rolling his eyes.@g]
Cy threw the heavy backpack of gold coins onto the counter.
"This bag is full of money," he told the clerk.
"Cy!" Bobby said, suddenly running into the store.
"I need some money for my car."
[g@Cy pushed his brother away.
"Not now, Bobby. I'm busy!" he said.@g]
[g@"But I found the car I want!" Bobby said.
He tried to grab the bag.@g]
[g@Cy shoved Bobby.
"I'll give it to you after I pay for my games!" he said.@g]
"It's my money too!" yelled Bobby.
Back at Dot's, Panther and Jane were not speaking to each other.
"This is a very pretty dress," said Dot, the owner of the shop.
[g@"Thank you. It's exactly what I wanted,"
Panther replied, but she was glaring at Jane.@g]
"I think it makes you look fat," Jane said in a mean voice.
[g@"You girls should be nice to each other.
Aren't you sisters?" Dot asked.@g]
But neither Panther nor Jane replied.
Meanwhile at the game store, Cy was ready to pay for his purchases.
"Your total comes to one thousand fifty-six dollars and seventy-one cents," the clerk said wearily.
Cy paused. "Uh, how much is that in gold coins?" he asked.
"Excuse me? Did you say gold coins?" asked the clerk.
[g@"Yes. That's what I have here."
Cy pointed to his bag.@g]
"Half of it's mine," Bobby said angrily.
"I'm sorry," the clerk said, "but we only accept cash, credit card, or check."
[g@"But these are worth a lot of money,"
Cy pleaded as he held out a coin.@g]
[g@"It looks like play money,"
the clerk said, taking the gold coin from him.@g]
[g@"They're real, I tell you,"
argued Cy, but the clerk did not believe him.@g]
[g@Jane felt like crying.
"It's not fair," she thought to herself.@g]
[g@"Why does Panther get to do whatever she wants?
I have money too."@g]
"That'll be twenty-one dollars and sixty cents," smiled Dot.
[g@"Fine," Panther replied.
She began counting out some gold coins.@g]
"Sweetie, we don't accept foreign currency here," Dot said.
[g@"These aren't foreign," laughed Panther.
"These are gold coins."@g]
[g@Dot picked one up suspiciously.
"Where did you get these?" she asked.@g]
Panther glanced over at Jane before answering.
[g@"From my uncle.
He gave them to us as a gift," Panther lied.@g]
Dot narrowed her eyes and stared at Panther.
[g@"Stay right here.
I'm going to make a phone call," she said.@g]
Then Dot disappeared into the back of the store.
[g@Panther grabbed Jane's arm and whispered frantically,
"Jane! I think she's going to call the police!"@g]
Jane crossed her arms and replied, "I don't care.
[g@You're the one in trouble, not me.
I didn't buy the dress."@g]
The situation at the game store wasn't looking any better.
"Come on, man." Cy continued to argue with the clerk.
"Look, I'll give you all the gold here.
That's going to be worth more than five thousand dollars!"
[g@"That's not fair!" shouted Bobby.
"Some of that is my money!@g]
[g@And I'm going to buy a car!"
Bobby grabbed the bag.@g]
"Let go, you little punk!" yelled Cy.
The boys began pulling and tugging at the bag.
Then, like a watermelon splitting open, the bag ripped in two, and the gold coins flew out everywhere.
At Dot's, Panther had to make a quick decision.
"Jane, we have to get out of here," she said.
When Jane didn't respond, Panther grabbed her arm and dragged her out of the store.
[g@"Get back here, girls!" Dot shouted, running toward them.
"I said, come back!"@g]
Without a backward glance, Panther and Jane ran off as fast as they could.
The clerk at the game store was very angry now.
"I'm going to call the cops," he threatened.
"For what?" Cy asked in a shaky voice.
"For trying to use counterfeit money," the clerk replied.
[g@"But this is real.
It's real gold, I tell you!"@g]
Cy argued, but it was all in vain.
Panther and Jane ran out of Dot's and didn't stop until they got to the game store.
"Are the police coming?" gasped Jane.
[g@Panther looked around.
"I don't think so.@g]
But we should find the boys and leave."
They didn't have to look long.
At that moment, Cy and Bobby came rushing out the door of the game store.
Behind them, the clerk was waving a fist and shouting threats.
